Incorporating the Beige Book alongside the FOMC statement and January 2018 SLOOS nudges the read more positive. The FOMC underscores a strengthened outlook, strong labor market, and gradual hikes, while SLOOS indicates supportive credit supply to businesses (easier or unchanged C&I standards, narrower spreads), with caution in CRE and some consumer categories. The Beige Book corroborates and amplifies the labor-side strength: districts report continued employment growth, strong demand for qualified workers, and rising wage pressure as employers raise wages and broaden compensation (with some influence from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act). That combination supports near-term growth and aligns with the FOMC’s expectation of inflation moving toward 2%. Offsets remain—labor shortages could constrain capacity, CRE standards are tighter with softer demand, and consumer credit shows mixed demand and expected performance—so risks still appear roughly balanced rather than unambiguously strong. Netting these, the Beige Book’s labor and wage signals tilt the assessment modestly more positive than before.
